title: Write claims that a reader can verify
summary: Describe the problem, one usable path, evidence and remaining limits.
objectives: Report implementation and test evidence at their actual scope.
Distinguish an unexecuted integration from a passing unit test.

sources.title: Rust Book: test organization
sources.basis: Unit and integration tests serve different scopes. The lesson applies that distinction to honest documentation, without claiming a Rust runtime was tested.

sections.title: Start with a concrete reader task
paragraphs: Explain the problem and intended user, then show one reproducible usage path, responsibilities and constraints. Label implemented, experimental and absent behavior.
Keep English and Japanese explanations on separate pages. Preserve upstream authorship and do not invent personal adoption dates or outcomes.

sections.title: Tie each result to its evidence
paragraphs: The synthetic report has a passed unit result and a not-run integration result. It must report the integration as unverified. A merged PR is not proof of production behavior.
Record commands, environment and bounds. Preserve useful failed experiments as history, without presenting old configurations as current recommendations.

exercise.instruction: Run the evidence-reporting example with not-run and failed integration results.
exercise.expected: Neither result is promoted to integration passed by a passing unit test.

limitations: This is an editorial exercise, not certification of every repository or its deployed service.
Published claims require review of evidence, scope and permission to disclose.
